seen_animation: A cartoon mouth drawn as an upper row of teeth inside a curved outline and a lower row of teeth inside a deeper curved jaw, with grey scenery lines above. Frames 1-2 the mouth is open with both rows of teeth separated. Frames 3-5 the lower jaw rises and the mouth closes until the lower teeth sit just under the upper row. Frames 6-8 it opens again, and frames 9-16 it holds a wide open mouth with the lower jaw dropped. Frame 17 it starts closing, frames 18-21 it is shut and flattened, and frames 22-26 it opens again into the wide open mouth and holds.
seen_film: A close-up of a man's mouth speaking and smiling. Frames 1-2 the lips are parted showing both rows of teeth. Frames 3-5 the lips close, fully shut by frame 5. Frames 6-10 the lips part slightly and push forward (pursed), showing only a little of the upper teeth. Frames 11-13 the mouth opens wide showing upper and lower teeth, frames 14-16 it settles into an open smile. Frame 17 the lips come together, frames 18-21 the mouth is closed, and frames 22-26 it opens into a broad toothy smile and holds.
named_subject: A cartoon mouth (upper and lower rows of teeth in a jaw outline) speaking and smiling.
evidence: Judged from still frames only. The close-open-close-open rhythm matches the film at the same frames: the mouth closes over e3-e5 as the film lips close at f3-f5; it is shut at e18-e21 exactly where the film is closed at f18-f21; it reopens at e22 when the film breaks into the smile at f22, and holds open through e26 as the film holds through f26. g.png shows the drawing staying in one place and only the lower jaw travelling up and down, which matches the film where the mouth does not travel across the frame. The drawing keeps c.png's construction in every frame: square-cornered upper teeth with pointed gaps, four tall lower teeth, the curved jaw line and the separate stroke on the right side. Consecutive frames change by small steps; the larger change e21-e22 matches the equally large change f21-f22.
primary_gap: In e6-e10 the mouth is already open wide while the film at f6-f10 is only slightly parted with pursed lips, so the second opening arrives about three frames early and is larger than the film's.
closes_when: e6-e10 show the lower jaw only slightly dropped below the upper teeth (a narrow gap like e3), with the full wide opening first reached at e11-e13.
protect: Keep the doodle's construction (square upper teeth with pointed gaps, four tall lower teeth, single curved jaw outline, the extra right-side stroke), the fixed position of the upper row, the closures at e3-e5 and e18-e21, the reopening at e22, and the small frame-to-frame jaw steps.
identity_gap: The character reads as the c.png teeth drawing throughout; the only change is the lower jaw being squashed flat in the closed frames, which still keeps its tooth strokes.
